verses.synonyms: kṛṣṇa—O Kṛṣṇa; tvadīya—our; pada-paṅkaja—of the lotus feet; pañjara—the network; antam—inside; adya—today; eva—certainly; viśatu—may enter; me—my; mānasa—of my mind; rāja-haṁsaḥ—the swan; prāṇa-prayāṇa—the departure of my life; samaye—at the time of; kapha—by mucus; vāta—bodily air; pittaiḥ—and bile; kaṇṭha—of the throat; avarodhana—the choking of the breath; vidhau—in that condition; smaraṇam—the memory; kuta—how will it be possible; te—of You.
verses.translation: My Lord Kṛṣṇa, I pray that the swan of my mind may immediately sink down to the stems of the lotus feet of Your Lordship and be locked up in their network; otherwise at the time of my final breath, when my throat is choked up with cough, how will it be possible to think of You?

verses.title: Prabodhānanda Sarasvatī from Caitanya-candrāmṛta
verses.text:
dante nidhāya tṛṇakaṁ padayor nipatya
kṛtvā ca kāku-śatam etad ahaṁ bravīmi
he sādhavaḥ sakalam eva vihāya dūrād
caitanya-candra-caraṇe kurutānurāgam
verses.synonyms: dante—between the teeth; nidhāya—placing; tṛṇakam—a blade of grass; padayor— your feet; nipatya—falling down; kṛtvā—having done; ca—and; kākuśatam—a hundred times flattering; etat—this; aham—I; bravīmi—submit; he sādhavaḥ—O great personality; sakalam—completely; eva—indeed; vihāya—leaving aside; dūrāt— at a distance; caitanya-candra-caraṇe—the lotus feet of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu; kuruta—just get; anurāgam—a taste for.
verses.translation: Taking a straw between my teeth and falling at your feet a hundred times, I humbly submit, "O great personality, please give up all mundane knowledge that you have learned and just submit yourself at the lotus feet of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu."

verses.title: Prabodhānanda Sarasvatī from Caitanya-candrāmṛta 5
verses.text:
kaivalyaṁ narakāyate tri-daśa-pūr ākāśa-puṣpāyate
durdāntendriya-kāla-sarpa-paṭalī protkhāta-daṁṣṭrāyate
viśvaṁ pūrṇa-sukhāyate vidhi-mahendrādiś ca kīṭāyate
yat kāruṇya-kaṭākṣa-vaibhavavatāṁ taṁ gauram eva stumaḥ
verses.synonyms: kaivalyam—the pleasure of merging into the existence of Brahman; narakāyate—is considered hellish; tri-daśa-pūr—the heavenly planets; ākāśa-puṣpāyate—something imaginary, like a flower in the sky; durdānta—formidable; indriya—the senses; kāla-sarpa—venomous snake; paṭalī—multitude; protkhāta—extracted; daṁṣṭrāyate— teeth; viśvam—the material world; pūrṇa—completely; sukhāyate—happy; vidhi— Lord Brahmā; mahendra—Indra, the king of heaven; ādiḥ—the demigods; ca—and; kīṭāyate—become like an insect; yat—of whom; kāruṇya—mercy; kaṭākṣa—glance; vaibhavavatām—of the most confidential devotee; tam—unto; gauram—Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu; eva—certainly; stumaḥ—glorify.
verses.translation: For a devotee, the pleasure of merging into the existence of Brahman is considered hellish. Similarly, he considers promotion to heavenly planets just another kind of phantasmagoria. The yogīs meditate for sense control, but for the devotee the senses appear like serpents with broken teeth. The whole material world appears joyful for a devotee, and even great personalities like Lord Brahmā and Lord Indra are considered no better than insects. Such is the position of a devotee who has received but a small glance of the mercy of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Unto this most magnanimous personality I offer my respectful obeisances.

verses.title: Śaṅkarācārya
verses.text:
bhaja govindaṁ bhaja govindaṁ bhaja govindaṁ mūḍha-mate
samprāpte sannihite kāle na hi na hi rakṣati dukṛñ-karaṇe
verses.synonyms: bhaja—just worship; govindam—Govinda; mūḍha-mate—O fool; samprāpte— attained; sannihite—placed; kāle—when the time; na—not; hi—indeed; rakṣati— protects; dukṛn-karaṇe—the grammatical affix dukṛn.
verses.translation: You fools and rascals, all your grammatical word jugglery of suffixes, prefixes and philosophical speculation will not save you at the time of death. Just worship Govinda! Worship Govinda! Worship Govinda!

verses.title: Śaṅkarācārya
verses.text:
nārī-stana-bhara-nābhī-deśaṁ
dṛṣṭvā mā gā mohā-veśam
etan māṁsa-vasādi-vikāraṁ
manasi vicintaya vāraṁ vāram
verses.synonyms: nāri—a woman's; stanā—breasts; bhāram—heavy; nābhi-deśam—waist; dṛṣṭvā— seeing; mā-gā—don't go; moha—illusion, attraction; veśyām—by such a woman; etām—these; māmsa—flesh, fat; vāsaḥ—outward dress; ādi—etc.; vikarā— transformation; manasi—in your mind; vicintāya—you should consider; bhāram— seriously; bhāram—very seriously.
verses.translation: Having seen the supposed beauty of a woman's heavy breasts and her thin waist, do not become agitated and illusioned, for these attractive features are simply transformations of fat, flesh and various other disgusting ingredients. You should consider this in your mind again and again.

verses.title: Śaṅkarācārya
verses.text: brahma satyaṁ jagan mithyā
verses.synonyms: brahma—Brahman, the Supreme Spirit; satyam—is truth; jagat—the material world; mithyā-is false.
verses.translation: The Supreme Brahman is the only truth, and this material world is false.

verses.title: Śaṅkarācārya Gītā-bhāṣya
verses.text: nārāyaṇa paro 'vyaktāt
verses.synonyms: nārāyaṇa—Nārāyaṇa, the Supreme Personality of Godhead; paraḥ—beyond, or superior to; avyaktāt—the unmanifested source of the material creation.
verses.translation: The Supreme Personality of Godhead, Nārāyaṇa, is beyond the material creation.

verses.title: Svarūpa Dāmodara
verses.text: bhāgavata giyā porā bhāgavata-sthāne
verses.synonyms: bhāgavata—Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam; giyā—going; porā—study; bhāgavata—devotees; sthāne—at the place.
verses.translation: One should hear and study the Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam from the "person Bhāgavatam".

verses.title: Yāmunācārya
verses.text:
yad-avadhi mama cetaḥ kṛṣṇa-pādāravinde
nava-nava-rasa-dhāmany udyataṁ rantum āsīt
tad-avadhi bata nārī-saṅgame smaryamāne
bhavati mukha-vikāraḥ suṣṭu niṣṭhīvanaṁ ca
verses.synonyms: yad-avadhi—ever since; mama—my; cetaḥ—mind; kṛṣṇa-pāda-āravinde—at the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa; nava-nava—newer and newer; rasa-dhāmani—the glories of transcendental taste; udyata—has arisen; rantum—to enjoy; āsīt—was; tad-avadhi— since then; bata—ah!; nārī-saṅgame—the association of women for sense gratification; smaryamāne—being remembered; bhavati—it becomes; mukha-vikāraḥ—lips or face contorted in disgust; suṣṭu—exceedingly; niṣṭhīvanam—in the act of spitting; ca—and.
verses.translation: Since my mind has been engaged in the transcendental loving service of Kṛṣṇa, realizing ever-new pleasure in Him, whenever I think of sex pleasure, I spit at the thought and my lips curl with distaste.

verses.title: Yāmunācārya Stotra-ratna 43
verses.text:
bhavantam evānucaran nirantaraḥ
praśānta-niḥśeṣa-mano-rathāntaraḥ
kadāham aikāntika-nitya-kiṅkaraḥ
praharṣayiṣyāmi sanātha-jīvitam
verses.synonyms: bhavantam—You; eva—certainly; anucaran—serving; nirantaraḥ—always; praśānta—pacified; niḥśeṣa—all; manaḥ-ratha—desires; antaraḥ—other; kadā— when; aham—I; aikāntika—exclusive; nitya—eternal; kiṅkaraḥ—servant; praharṣayiṣyāmi—I shall become joyful; sa-nātha—with a fitting master; jīvitam— living.
verses.translation: By serving You constantly, one is freed from all material desires and is completely pacified. When shall I engage as Your permanent eternal servant and always feel joyful to have such a fitting master?

verses.title: Aruṇodaya-kīrtana 1.1
verses.text:
udila aruṇa pūraba-bhāge
dvija-maṇi gorā amani jāge
verses.synonyms: udila—rising; aruṇa—the redness that preceeds the rising sun; pūraba—eastern; bhāge—quarter; dvija-maṇi—jewel of the twiceborn; gorā—Lord Caitanya; amani— Himself; jāge—awakened.
verses.translation: When a tinge of red on the eastern horizon heralded the sunrise, the jewel of the twiceborn, Lord Gaurasundara, immediately awakened. Taking His devotees with Him, He went all over the countryside, visiting the towns and villages of Nadia.

verses.title: Aruṇodaya-kīrtana 1.6
verses.text:
jīvana anitya jānaha sār
tāhe nānā-vidha vipada-bhār,
nāmāśraya kori' jatane tumi
thākaha āpana kāje
verses.synonyms: jīvana—life; anitya—temporary; jānaha—know; sār—in truth; tāhe—in that; nānā-vidha—various kinds of; vipada-bhār—dangers; nāmāśraya kori'—take shelter of the holy name; jatane—carefully; tumi—you; thākaha—remain; āpana—in your own; kāje—activities.
verses.translation: "Understand this essential fact of life: life is temporary and full of all kinds of miseries. So take shelter of the holy name as your only business."

verses.title: Aruṇodaya-kīrtana 2.1
verses.text:
jīv jāgo, jīv jāgo, gauracānda bole
kota nidrā jāo māyā-piśācīra kole
verses.synonyms: jīva—O living entity; jāga—wake up; gauracānda—Lord Caitanya; bole—calls; kota—how long; nidrā jāo—you sleep; māyā-piśācīra—of the witch Māyā; kole—in the lap.
verses.translation: Lord Gaurāṅga is calling, "Wake up, sleeping souls! Wake up, sleeping souls! You have slept so long in the lap of the witch Māyā."

verses.title: Śaraṇāgati
verses.text:
mānasa, deho, geho, jo kichu mora
arpilū tuyā pade, nanda-kiśora!
verses.synonyms: mānasa—mind; deho—body; geho—family; jo—whatever; kichu—little; mora— mine; arpilū—offered; tuyā—Your; pade—to the feet; nanda-kiśora—O youthful son of Nanda.
verses.translation: Mind, body and family, whatever may be mine, I have surrendered at Your lotus feet, O youthful son of Nanda!

verses.title: Śaraṇāgati
verses.text:
mārobi rākhobi-yo icchā tohārā
nitya-dāsa prati tuyā adhikārā
verses.synonyms: mārobi—kill; rākhobi—protect; yo—whatever; icchā—desire; tohārā—Your; nitya-dāsa—eternal servant; prati—towards; tuyā—You; adhikārā—owner.
verses.translation: Slay me or protect me as You wish, for You are the master of Your eternal servant.

verses.title: Śaraṇāgati
verses.text:
kīṭa-janma hau yathā tuyā dāsa
bahir-mukha brahma-janme nāhi āśa
verses.synonyms: kīṭa—worm; janma—birth; hau—let it be; jathā—so long as; tuyā—Your; dāsa— servant; bahir-mukha—adverse; brahma-janme—born as Brahmā; nāhi—not; āśa— become.
verses.translation: Let me be born again even as a worm, as long as I may remain Your devotee. I have no desire to be born as a Brahmā averse to You.

verses.title: Śaraṇāgati
verses.text:
ye dina gṛhe, bhajana dekhi,
gṛhete goloka bhāya
caraṇa-sīdhu, dekhiyā gaṅgā
sukha nā sīmā pāya
verses.synonyms: ye dina—when; gṛhe—at home; bhajana—the worship; dekhi—I see; gṛhete—in the home; goloka—Goloka Vṛndāvana; bhāya—appears; caraṇa—the lotus feet of the Lord; sīdhu—the nectar; dekhiyā gaṅgā—upon seeing the Ganges; sukha—happiness; nā—no; sīmā—limits; pāya—does not find.
verses.translation: Every day Goloka Vṛndāvana appears in my home when I see Lord Hare being worshiped there. My joy knows no bounds when I see the Ganges, a river of nectar emanating from the Lord's lotus feet.

verses.title: Prasāda-sevāya From Gītāvalī
verses.text:
śarīra avidyā-jāl, joḍendriya tāhe kāl,
jīve phele viṣaya-sāgore
tā'ra madhye jihvā ati, lobhamoy sudurmati,
tā'ke jetā kaṭhina saṁsāre

kṛṣṇa baḍo doyāmay, karibāre jihvā jay,
sva-prasād-anna dila bhāi
sei annāmṛta pāo, rādhā-kṛṣṇa-guṇa gāo,
preme ḍāko caitanya-nitāi
verses.translation: O Lord, this material body is a place of ignorance, and the senses are a network of paths leading to death. Somehow we have fallen into this ocean of material sense enjoyment, and of all the senses the tongue is the most voracious and uncontrollable. It is very difficult to conquer the tongue in this world. But You, dear Kṛṣṇa, are very kind to us and have given us such nice prasādam just to control the tongue. Now we take this prasādam to our full satisfaction and glorify You-Śrī Śrī Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa-and in love call for the help of Lord Caitanya and Nityānanda.

verses.title: Iṣṭa-deve Vijñapti 1
verses.text:
hari hari! biphale janama goṅāinu
manuṣya-janama pāiyā, rādhā-kṛṣṇa nā bhajiyā,
jāniyā śuniyā biṣa khāinu
verses.synonyms: hari—O Lord Hari; biphale—uselessly; janama—my life; goṅāinu—I have spent; manuṣya-janama—human birth; pāiyā—having obtained; rādhā-kṛṣṇa—Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa; nā—not; bhajiyā—worshiping; jāniyā—having understood; śuniyā—having heard; biṣa—poison; khāinu—I have drunk.
verses.translation: O Lord Hari, I have wasted my life. Although I have taken this rare human birth, like a miser, I have not served Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa, and thus I have knowingly drunk poison.

verses.title: Iṣṭa-deve Vijñapti 2 from Prārthanā
verses.text:
golokera prema-dhana, hari-nāma-saṅkīrtana,
rati nā janmilo kene tāya
saṁsāra-biṣānaledibā-niśi hiyā jvale
juḍāite nā koinu upāya
verses.synonyms: golokera—of Goloka Vṛndāvana; prema-dhana—the treasure of love for Kṛṣṇa; hari-nāma-saṅkīrtana—the glorification of the holy name of Lord Hari; rati—attraction; nā—not; janmilo—manifest; kene—why; tāya saṁsāra—of material existence; biṣa—of poison; anale—in the fire; dibā-niśi—day and night; hiyā jvale—burns; juḍāite—spreads; nā—not; koinu—spreads; upāya—the remedy.
verses.translation: The treasure of divine love in Goloka Vṛndāvana has descended as the congregational chanting of Lord Hari's holy names. Why did my attraction for that chanting never come about? Day and night my heart burns in the fire of the poison of worldliness, and I have not accepted the means for relieving it.

verses.title: Iṣṭa-deve Vijñapti 3 from Prārthanā
verses.text:
brajendra-nandana yei, śacī-suta hoilo sei,
balarāma hoilo nitāi
dīna-hīna yata chilo, hari-nāme uddhārilo,
tāra śākṣī jagāi mādhāi
verses.synonyms: braja—of Vraja; indra—of the king; nandana—the son; yei—who is; śacī-suta—the son of mother Śacī; hoilo—has become; sei—He is; balarāma—Balarāma; hoilo—has become; nitāi—Lord Nityānanda; dīna—poor; hīna—and fallen; yata—who; chilo— were; hari-nāme—the name of Lord Hari; uddhārilo—were delivered; tāra—of this; śākṣi—testimony; jagāi—Jagāi; mādhāi—Mādhāi.
verses.translation: Lord Kṛṣṇa, the son of the King of Vraja, became the son of Śacī, and Balarāma became Nitāi. The holy name delivered all those souls who were lowly and wretched. The two sinners Jagāi and Mādhāi are evidence of this.

verses.title: Iṣṭa-deve Vijñapti 4 from Prārthanā
verses.text:
hā hā prabhu nanda-suta, vṛṣabhānu-sutā-yuta,
karuṇā karoho ei-bāro
narottama-dāsa kaya, nā ṭheliho rāṅgā pāya,
tomā bine ke āche āmāra
verses.synonyms: hā—O; hā—O; prabhu—Lord; nanda-suta—son of Nanda Mahārāja; vṛṣabhānu-sutā—the daughter of Mahārāja Vṛṣabhānu; yuta—accompanied; karuṇā—mercy; karoho—please give; ei-bāro—this time; narottama-dāsa—Narottama dāsa; kaya— says; nā—do not; ṭheliho—push away; rāṅgā—reddish lotus feet; pāya—having attained; tomā—for You; bine—except; ke—who; āche—is; āmāra—mine.
verses.translation: O Lord Kṛṣṇa, son of Nanda, accompanied by the daughter of Vṛṣabhānu, please be merciful to me now. Narottama dāsa says, "O Lord, please do not push me away from Your reddish lotus feet, for who is my beloved except for You?"

verses.title: Lālasā-mayī Prārthanā 1
verses.text:
'gaurāṅga' bolite habe pulaka-śarīra
'hari hari' bolite nayane ba'be nīra
verses.synonyms: gaurāṅga—Gaurāṅga; bolite—saying; habe—will; pulaka—with shivering; śarīra— body; hari—O Hari; hari—O Hari; bolite—saying; nayane—on the eyes; ba'be— flaws; nīra—tears.
verses.translation: When will that opportune moment come to us when there will be shivering of the body as soon as we chant Lord Gaurāṅga's name? While chanting Hare Kṛṣṇa, when will there be tears in our eyes?

verses.title: Lālasā-mayī Prārthanā 2
verses.text:
āra kabe nitāi-cānder karuṇā hoibe
saṁsāra-bāsanā mora kabe tuccha ha'be
verses.synonyms: āra—and; kabe—will be; nitāi—of Lord Nityānanda; cānder—of the moon; karuṇā—mercy; hoibe—will be; saṁsāra—of material existence; bāsanā—the desire; mora—my; kabe—when; tuccha—insignificant; ha'be—will be.
verses.translation: When will I obtain the mercy of Lord Nityānandacandra? When, by His mercy will the desire for material enjoyment become insignificant?

verses.title: Lālasā-mayī Prārthanā 3
verses.text:
viṣaya chāḍiyā kabe śuddha ha'be mana
kabe hāma herabo śrī-vṛndāvana
verses.synonyms: viṣaya—material sense gratification; chāḍiyā—giving up; kabe—when; śuddha— when; ha'be—will be; mana—the mind; kabe—when; hāma—I; herabo—I will see; śrī-vṛndāvana—Śrī Vṛndāvana-dhāma.
verses.translation: When will my mind become free from all material desires and anxieties? Only in that purified state will I be able to understand Vṛndāvana and the conjugal love of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa. Then my spiritual life will be successful.

verses.title: Lālasā-mayī Prārthanā 4
verses.text:
rūpa-raghunātha-pade hoibe ākuti
kabe hāma bujhabo se yugala-pīriti
verses.synonyms: rūpa—Rūpa Gosvāmī; raghunātha—Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī; pade—the books; hoibe—will be; ākuti—eagerness; kabe—when; hāma—I; bujhabo—I will understand; se—this; yugala—the divine couple; pīriti—love.
verses.translation: When shall I be very much eager to study the books left by the Six Gosvāmīs, headed by Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī and Śrīla Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī? By their instruction I shall be able to properly understand the loving affairs of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa.

verses.title: Nāma-saṅkīrtana 6
verses.text:
ei chaya gosāi yāra-mui tāra dāsa
tāṅ'-sabāra pada-reṇu mora pañca-grāsa
verses.synonyms: ei—that one; chaya—six; gosāi—Gosvāmī; yāra—a lover; mui—I; tāra—of him; dāsa—servant; tāṅ'—them; sabāra—of all; pada—feet; reṇu—dust; mora—my; pañca—five; grāsa—foodstuffs.
verses.translation: I am the servant of that person who is a servant of the Six Gosvāmīs. The dust of their holy feet is my five kinds of foodstuffs.

verses.title: Nāma-saṅkīrtana 7
verses.text:
tāndera caraṇa sevi-bhakta-sane vāsa
janame janame hoy ei abhilāṣa
verses.synonyms: tāndera—of them (the Six Gosvāmīs); caraṇa—feet; sevi—servants; bhakta— devotees; sane—in association; vāsa—live; janame janame—birth after birth; hoy— is; ei—this; abhilāsa—desire.
verses.translation: This is my desire, that birth after birth I may live with those devotees who serve the lotus feet of the Six Gosvāmīs.

verses.title: Prema-bhakti-candrikā
verses.text: chāḍiyā vaiṣṇava-sevā nistara payeche kebā
verses.synonyms: chāḍiyā—giving up; vaiṣṇava-sevā—service of the Vaiṣṇavas; nistara—firm faith; payeche—will not get liberation; kebā—someone.
verses.translation: Unless one serves the spiritual master and the acāryas one cannot get liberation.

verses.title: Prema-bhakti-candrikā
verses.text:
karma-kāṇḍa, jñāna-kāṇḍa, kevala viṣera bhāṇḍa,
'amṛta' baliyā yebā khāya
nānā yoni sadā phire, kadarya bhakṣaṇa kare,
tāra janma adhaḥ-pāte yāya
verses.synonyms: karma-kāṇḍa—fruitive activities; jñāna-kāṇḍa—philosophical speculation described in the Vedas; kevala—only; viṣera—of poison; bhāṇḍa—containers; amṛta—nectar; baliyā—saying; yebā—whoever; khāya—eats; nānā—various; yoni—species; sadā— always; phire—stays; kadarya—abominable substances or stool; bhakṣaṇa—teaching; kare—does; tāra—his; janma—birth; adhaḥ-pāte—falling down; yāya—attaining.
verses.translation: Fruitive activities and mental speculation are simply cups of poison. Whoever drinks of them, thinking them to be nectar, must struggle very hard life after life, in different types of bodies. Such a person eats all kinds of nonsense and becomes condemned by his activities of so-called sense enjoyment.

verses.title: Prema-bhakti-candrikā
verses.text: sadhu śāstra guru vākya, cittete kariyā aikya
verses.synonyms: sadhu—saintly persons; śāstra—the holy scriptures; guru—the bona fide spiritual master; vākya—the words of; cittete—in the heart; kariyā—having done; aikya—one (nondifferent).
verses.translation: We must always keep within our hearts the instructions of sādhu, śāstra, and guru. This is the process.

verses.title: Prema-bhakti-candrikā
verses.text:
'kāma' kṛṣṇa-kārmārpaṇe 'krodha' bhakta-dweśi-jane
'lobha' sādhu-saṅge hari-kathā
'moha' iṣṭa-labha-bine 'mada' kṛṣṇa-guṇa-gāne
niyukta kariba yathā tathā
verses.synonyms: kāma—lust; kṛṣṇa—to Lord Kṛṣṇa; kārma—deeds; arpaṇe—in offering; krodha— anger; bhakta—devotees; dweśi-jane—towards the enemies; lobha—greed; sādhu-saṅge—the association of saintly devotees; hari-kathā—the glories of Lord Hari; moha—bewilderment; iṣṭa—worshipable; labha—attainment; bine—without; mada—madness; kṛṣṇa—Lord Kṛṣṇa; guṇa—qualities; gāne—in glorifying; niyukta kariba—I will engage; yathā—as; tathā—in that way.
verses.translation: I will engage my lust by offering the fruits of my work to Lord Kṛṣṇa, and I will engage my anger by directing it at those who are envious of the lord's devotees. I will engage greed by becoming greedy to hear the glories of the Lord in the association of saintly devotees. By not attaining my worshipable Lord Kṛṣṇa, I will engage the quality of bewilderment; and I will engage madness by becoming mad to glorify the transcendental qualities of the Lord. In this way I will spiritualize these material qualities for the service of the Lord.

verses.title: Sāvaraṇa-śrī-gaura-pāda-padme from Prārthanā-1
verses.text:
śrī-kṛṣṇa-caitanya-prabhu dayā koro more
tomā binā ke dayālu jagat-saṁsāre
verses.synonyms: śrī-kṛṣṇa-caitanya—Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya; prabhu—O Lord; doyā—mercy; koro— please do; more—to me; tomā—You; binā—except for; ke—who?; dayālu—is merciful; jagat-saṁsāre—in this material world.
verses.translation: My dear Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya Mahāprabhu, please be merciful to me, because who can be more merciful that Your Lordship within these three worlds?

verses.title: Sāvaraṇa-śrī-gaura-pāda-padme from Prārthanā-2
verses.text:
patita-pāvana-hetu tava avatāra
mo sama patita prabhu nā pāibe āra
verses.synonyms: patita-pāvana—deliverer of the most fallen; hetu—the reason; tava—Your; avatāra—incarnation; mo sama—like me; patita—fallen; prabhu—O Lord; nā—not; pāibe—there; āra—another.
verses.translation: Your incarnation is just to reclaim the conditioned, fallen souls, but I assure You that You will not find a greater candidate for Your mercy than me.

verses.title: Sāvaraṇa-śrī-gaura-pāda-padme from Prārthanā-3
verses.text:
hā hā prabhu nityānanda, premānanda sukhī
kṛpābalokana koro āmi boḍo duḥkhī
verses.synonyms: hā—O; hā—O; prabhu—Lord; nityānanda—Nityānanda; premānanda—spiritual bliss; sukhī—joyful; kṛpa—of mercy; balokana—glance; koro—please do; āmi—I; boḍo—very; duḥkhī—unhappy.
verses.translation: O my dear Lord Nityānanda! Since You are always very joyful in spiritual bliss, please cast Your merciful glance over me, because I am very unhappy.

verses.title: Sāvaraṇa-śrī-gaura-mahimā from Prārthanā
verses.text:
gaurāṅgera saṅgi-gaṇe, nitya-siddha kori' māne,
se yāya-vrajendra-sūta-pāśa
verses.synonyms: gaurāṅgera—of Lord Gaurāṅga; saṅgi-gaṇe—the associates; nitya-siddha—perfect; kori'—doing; māne—in the mind; se—he; yāya—attaining; braja-indra-sūta—the prince of Vraja; pāśa—nearness.
verses.translation: Simply by understanding that the associates of Lord Caitanya are eternally free from material contamination, one can immediately be promoted to the transcendental abode of Lord Kṛṣṇa.

verses.title: Sāvaraṇa-śrī-gaura-mahimā from Prārthanā
verses.text:
śrī-gauḍa-maṇḍala-bhūmi, yebā jāne cintāmaṇi,
tāra haya vraja-bhūme bāsa
verses.synonyms: śrī-gauḍa-maṇḍala-bhūmi—the land where Lord Caitanya performed pastimes; yebā—whoever; jāne—understands; cintāmaṇi—transcendental abode; tāra—of him; haya—is; vraja-bhūme—in Vrajabhūmi; vāsa—residence.
verses.translation: If one simply understands that the land of Navadvīpa is not different from Vṛndāvana, he actually lives in Vṛndāvana.

verses.title: Śrī Guru-vandanā 2 from Prema-bhakti-candrikā
verses.text:
guru-mukha-padma-vākya, cittete koriyā-aikya,
ār nā koriho mane āśā
verses.synonyms: guru-mukha-padma-vākya—the instructions emanating from the lotus mouth of the spiritual master; cittete—in the consciousness; koriyā-aikya—making exclusively established; ār—anything else; nā—not; koriho mane āśā—do not aspire for.
verses.translation: My only wish is to have my consciousness purified by the words emanating from his lotus mouth.

verses.title: Śrī Guru-vandanā from Prema-bhakti-candrikā
verses.text:
cakhu-dān dilo yei, janme janme prabhu sei,
divya-jñāna hṛde prokāśito
verses.synonyms: cakhu—of the eyes; dāna—gift; dila—gives; yei—who; janme janme—birth after birth; prabhu—master; sei—he; divya—transcendental; jñāna—knowledge; hṛde—in the heart; prokāśita—manifests.
verses.translation: The spiritual master opens my darkened eyes and fills my heart with transcendental knowledge. He is my lord birth after birth.

verses.title: Gītā Govinda Daśāvatāra-stotra 4
verses.text:
tava kara-kamala-vare nakham adbhuta-śṛṅgaṁ
dalita-hiraṇyakaśipu-tanu-bhṛṅgam
keśava dhṛta-narahari-rūpa jaya jagadīśa hare
verses.synonyms: tava—Your; kara-kamala—lotuslike hands; vare nakham—nails; adbhuta— wonderful; śṛṅga—pointed; dalita—killed; hiraṇyakaśipu—Hiryaṇyakaśipu; tanu-bhṛṅgam—body like a wasp; keśava—Lord Kṛṣṇa; dhṛta—assuming; narahari-rūpa— the form of half-man, half-lion; jaya—all glories; jagadīśa—Lord of the universe; hare—O Hari.
verses.translation: O Keśava! O Lord of the universe! O Lord Hari, who have assumed the form of a half-man, half-lion! All glories to You! with the wonderfully sharp nails on Your beautiful lotus hands You have ripped apart the wasplike body of Hiraṇyakaśipu.

verses.title: Gītā Govinda Daśāvatāra-stotra 9
verses.text:
nindāsī yajña-vidher ahaha śruti-jātaṁ
sadaya-hṛdaya darśita-paśu-ghātaṁ
keśava dhṛta-buddha-śarīra jaya jagadīśa hare
verses.synonyms: nindāsī—decrying; yajña-vidher—animal sacrifice; ahaha—completely; śruti-jātam— Vedic rituals; sadaya-hṛdaya—heart full of compassion; darśita—upon seeing; paśu-ghātam—killing of animals; keśava—Lord Kṛṣṇa; dhṛta—assuming; buddha-śarīra— the form of Lord Buddha; jaya—all glories; jagadīśa—Lord of the universe; hare—O Hari.
verses.translation: O Keśava! O Lord of the universe! O Lord Hari, who have assumed the form of Buddha! All glories to You! With your heart full of compassion, you decry animal slaughter performed according to the scriptural rules of Vedic sacrifice.

verses.title: Nīti Śāstra
verses.text:
ātma-mātā guroḥ patnī
brāhmaṇī rāja-patnikā
dhenur dhātrī tathā pṛthvī
saptaitā mātaraḥ smṛtāḥ
verses.synonyms: ātma-mātā—one's own mother; guroḥ-patnī—the wife of the guru; brāhmaṇi—the wife of a brāhmaṇa; rāja-patnikā—the wife of a king; dhenuḥ—the cow; dhātrī—the nurse; tathā—thus; pṛthvī—the earth; sapta etā—these seven; mātaraḥ—mothers; smṛtāḥ—should be remembered as.
verses.translation: One's own mother, the wife of the guru, the wife of a brāhmaṇa, the wife of a king, the cow, the nurse, and the earth are known as the seven mothers of a man.

verses.title: Nīti Śāstra
verses.text:
avidyaṁ jīvanaṁ śūnyaṁ
dik-śūnyāś ca abāndhavāḥ
putra-hīnaṁ gṛhaṁ śūnyaṁ
sarva-śūnyā daridratā
verses.synonyms: avidyam—without knowledge; jīvanam—life; śūnyam—empty or void; dik-śūnyāḥ— all directions are void; ca—and; abāndhavāḥ—persons without family or friends; putra-hīnam—without a son; gṛham—the home; śūnyam—void; sarva-śūnyā—that which makes everything void; daridratā—poverty.
verses.translation: Life without knowledge is empty, and all directions are void for those without friends. Household life without a son is void, and for the poor the whole world is void.

verses.title: Nīti Śāstra
verses.text:
āyuṣaḥ kṣaṇa eko 'pi
na labhya svarṇa-koṭibhiḥ
na cen nirarthakaṁ nītiḥ
kā ca hānis tato 'dhikā
verses.synonyms: āyuṣaḥ—of life; kṣanaḥ—a moment; ekaḥ—one; api—even; na—not; labhyaḥ— obtainable; svarṇa-koṭibhiḥ—for millions of gold coins; na cet—if not; nirarthakam— useless; nītiḥ—behavior; kā—what; ca—and; hāniḥ—loss; tataḥ—than that; adhikā—greater.
verses.translation: Even one moment of life spent cannot be regained for millions of gold coins. Therefore, what greater loss is there than time spent uselessly?

verses.title: Nīti Śāstra
verses.text:
durjanaḥ parihartavyo
vidyayālaṅkṛto 'pi san
maṇinā bhūṣitaḥ sarpaḥ
kim asau na bhayaṅkaraḥ
verses.synonyms: durjanaḥ—an evil man; parihartavyo—should be avoided; vidyaya—by knowledge; alaṅkṛtaḥ—decorated; api—although; san—being; maṇinā—by a jewel; bhūṣitaḥ— adorned; sarpaḥ—a snake; kim asau—is that; na—not; bhayaṅkaraḥ—fearful.
verses.translation: An evil man should be avoided, even though he may be decorated with great knowledge. He is just like a venomous serpent adorned with a jewel on his hood. Is not such a snake fearful?

verses.title: Nīti Śāstra
verses.text:
duṣṭā bhāryā śaṭhaṁ mitraṁ
bhṛtyaś cottaradāyakaḥ
sasarpe ca gṛhe vāso
mṛtyur eva na saṁśayaḥ
verses.synonyms: duṣṭā—wicked; bhāryā—wife; śaṭham—deceitful; mitram—friend; bhṛtyaḥ—servant; ca—and; uttara-dāyakaḥ—impertinent; sa-sarpe—with serpents; ca—and; gṛhe—in the house; vāsaḥ—residence; mṛtyuḥ—death; eva—certainly; na—not; saṁśayaḥ— doubt.
verses.translation: A man whose wife is wicked, whose friends are deceitful, and whose servants are impertinent dwells in a house infested with serpents. Death is certain.

verses.title: Nīti Śāstra
verses.text:
ekenāpi kuvṛkṣeṇa
koṭara-sthena vahninā
dahyate tad-vanaṁ sarvaṁ
kuputreṇa kulaṁ yathā
verses.synonyms: ekena—by one; api—only; ku-vṛkṣeṇa—bad tree; koṭara-sthena—in the hollow; vahninā—by a fire; dahyate—is burned; tat—of that; vanam—the forest; sarvam— entire; ku-putreṇa—by a bad son; kulam—family; yathā—just as.
verses.translation: Just as an entire forest is reduced to ashes by a fire burning in the hollow of a tree, similarly, one bad son can destroy an entire family.

verses.title: Nīti Śāstra
verses.text:
ko 'rthaḥ putreṇa jātena
yo na vidvān na dhārmikaḥ
kāneṇa cakṣuṣā kiṁ vā
cakṣuḥ pīḍaiva kevalam
verses.synonyms: kaḥ-arthaḥ—what is the value; putreṇa—with a son; jātena—born; yaḥ—who; na— not; vidvān—learned; na—not; dhārmikaḥ—religious; kāṇena-cakṣuṣā—with a blind eye; kiṁvā—or; cakṣuḥ—eye; piḍā—pain; eva—certainly; kevalam—only.
verses.translation: What is the value of a son who is neither learned nor religious? Such a son is compared to a blind eye that is only a source of pain.

verses.title: Nīti Śāstra
verses.text:
mātṛvat para-dāreṣu
para-dravyeṣu loṣṭravat
ātmavat sarva-bhūteṣu
yaḥ paśyati sa paṇḍitaḥ
verses.synonyms: mātṛvat—like one's mother; para-dāreṣu—others' wives; para-dravyeṣu—others' positions; loṣṭravat—like a lump of clay; ātmavat—like one's self; sarva-bhūteṣu—all living beings; yaḥ—who; paśyati—sees; saḥ—he; paṇḍitaḥ—a learned man.
verses.translation: One who sees others' wives as his mother, who sees all others' possessions as insignificant as a lump of clay, and who sees all living beings as himself-such a person is considered a learned man.

verses.title: Nīti Śāstra
verses.text:
lālayet pañca-varṣāṇi
daśa-varṣāṇi tāḍayet
prāpte tu ṣoḍaśe varṣe
putraṁ mitra-vad ācaret
verses.synonyms: lālayet—one should fondle; pañca-varṣāṇi—for five years; daśa-varṣāṇi—for ten years; tāḍayet—one should punish; prāpte—when he has reached; tu—but; ṣoḍaśe varṣe—the sixteenth year; putram—unto the son; mitra-vat—like a friend; ācaret— one should act.
verses.translation: One should fondle his son up to the point of five years old. Thereafter one should administer punishment for the next ten years. But when one's son reaches the age of sixteen one should act as a friend towards him.

verses.title: Nīti Śāstra
verses.text:
lālane bahavo doṣās
tāḍane bahavo guṇāḥ
tasmāt putraṁ ca śiṣyaṁ ca
tāḍayen na tu lālayet
verses.synonyms: lālane—in fondling; bahavaḥ—many; doṣāḥ—faults; tāḍane—in administering punishment; bahavaḥ—many; guṇāḥ—good qualities; tasmāt—therefore; putram—a son; ca—and; śiṣyam—a student; ca—and; tāḍayet—should punish; na—not; tu— but; lālayet—should fondle.
verses.translation: Leniency encourages bad qualities in a student or son, and strictness helps develop good qualities. Therefore, a teacher or parent should not pamper a child but administer punishment for bad behavior.

verses.title: Nīti Śāstra
verses.text:
mātā yasya gṛhe nāsti
bhāryā cāpriya-vādinī
araṇyaṁ tena gantavyaṁ
yathāraṇyaṁ tathā gṛham
verses.synonyms: mātā—an affectionate mother; yasya—who; gṛhe—in the home; na—not; asti— there is; bhāryā—a wife; ca—and; priya-vādinī—unkind, harsh speech; araṇyam— forest; tena—by him; gantavyam—one should go; yathā—so as; araṇyam—the forest; tathā—so; gṛham—the home.
verses.translation: If one does not have an affectionate mother at home or one's wife does not speak sweetly and lovingly one should go to the forest [take sannyāsa] because the home is already a desolate place.

verses.title: Nīti Śāstra
verses.text:
mūrkhā yatra na pūjyante
dhānyaṁ yatra susañcitam
dampatyoḥ kalaho nāsti
tatra śrīḥ svayam āgatāḥ
verses.synonyms: mūrkhā—fools; yatra—where na—not; pūjyante—are worshiped; dhānyam—grain; yatra—where; susañcitam—nicely stocked; dampatyoḥ—of husband and wife; kalaḥ—quarrel; na—not; asti—is; tatra—there; śrīḥ—goddess of fortune; svayam— personally; āgatāḥ—has come.
verses.translation: The goddess of fortune personally comes to that place where fools are not worshiped, where grains are carefully stocked, and where there are no quarrels between husband and wife.

verses.title: Nīti Śāstra
verses.text:
viṣād apy amṛtaṁ grāhyam
amedhyād api kāñcanam
nīcād apy uttamaṁ jñānaṁ
strī-ratnaṁ duṣkulād api
verses.synonyms: viṣād—from poison; api—even; amṛtam—nectar; grāhyam—is to be taken; amedhyāt—from an impure place; api—even; kāñcanam—gold; nīcāt—from a low-born person; api—even; uttamam—the best; jñānam—knowledge; strī-ratnam—a jewel of a woman; duṣkulāt—from a low family; api—even.
verses.translation: One would accept nectar even from poison and gold even from a filthy place. One should accept knowledge even from a low-born person, and a good wife even if she comes from a low family.

verses.title: Nīti Śāstra
verses.text:
ṛṣi śraddha ajā yuddhe
prabhāte megha garjane
dampatya kalahe caiva
bahvārambhe laghu kriyā
verses.synonyms: ṛṣi—sage; śraddha—funeral ceremony; ajā—male goat; yuddhe—fight; prabhāte—in the morning; megha—cloud; garjane—roar of thunder; dampatya—between husband and wife; kalahe—quarrel; ca—and; eva—certainly; bahu—grand; arambhe— beginning; laghu—small; kriyā—activity.
verses.translation: The funeral ceremony of a sage who died in the forest, a fight between two goats, a thunder clap in the morning, a quarrel between husband and wife-all begin in grand style but the outcome is insignificant.

verses.title: Nīti Śāstra
verses.text:
payaḥ-pānaṁ bhujaṅgānām
kevalaṁ viṣa-vardhanam
upadeśo hi mūrkhānāṁ
prakopāya na śāntaye
verses.synonyms: payaḥ-pānam—drinking milk; bhujaṅgānām—of the snakes; kevalam—only; viṣa-vardhanam—increasing the poison; upadeśaḥ—the instruction; hi—certainly; mūrkhānām—of fools; prakopāya—for anger; na—not; śāntaye—peace of mind.
verses.translation: When snakes drink milk, it only increases their venom. Similarly, good instructions offered to fools makes them angry, and does not give them peace of mind.

verses.title: Nīti Śāstra
verses.text:
rūpa-yauvana-sampannā
viśāla-kula-sambhavāḥ
vidyā-hīnā na śobhante
nirgandhā iva kiṁśukāh
verses.synonyms: rūpa—beauty; yauvana—youth; sampannāḥ—endowed with; viśāla-kula—in a high family; sambhavāḥ—persons who are born; vidyā-hīnāḥ—without knowledge; na śobhante—do not appear radiant; nirgandhāḥ—devoid of fragrance; iva—like; kiṁśukāḥ—the flowers of the Kimśuka tree.
verses.translation: Persons born in high families and endowed with beauty and youth do not appear complete if they are devoid of knowledge, just as the beautiful flowers of the Kimśuka tree do not appear attractive if they are devoid of fragrance.

verses.title: Nīti Śāstra
verses.text:
sarpaḥ krūraḥ khalaḥ krūraḥ
sarpāt krūrataraḥ khalaḥ
mantrauṣadhi-vaśaḥ sarpaḥ
khalaḥ kena nivāryate
verses.synonyms: sarpaḥ—a snake; krūraḥ—fierce; khalaḥ—an evil man; krūraḥ—fierce; sarpāt—than a snake; krūrataraḥ—more ferocious; khalaḥ—an evil man; mantra-auṣadhi—by mantras and herbs; vaśaḥ—controlled; sarpaḥ—a snake; khalaḥ—an evil man; kena—by what means; nivāryate—is controlled.
verses.translation: Snakes and wicked men are certainly dangerous, but of the two, a wicked man is more dangerous than a poisonous snake. A snake can be controlled by mantras and herbs, but how can an evil man be controlled?

verses.title: Nīti Śāstra
verses.text:
pṛthivī-bhūṣaṇaṁ rājā
nārīnāṁ bhūṣaṇaṁ patiḥ
śarvarī-bhūṣaṇaṁ candro
vidyā sarvasya bhūṣaṇam
verses.synonyms: pṛthivī-bhūṣaṇam—the ornament of the earth; rājā—is the king; nārīṇām—of women; bhūṣaṇam—the ornament; patiḥ—is the husband; śarvarī-bhūṣaṇam—the ornament of night; candro—is the moon; vidyā—knowledge; sarvasya—of everything; bhūṣaṇam—ornament.
verses.translation: The ornament of the earth is the king, and the ornament of a woman is a good husband. The ornament of night is the moon, and knowledge is the ornament of everything.

verses.title: Nīti Śāstra
verses.text:
tyaja durjana-saṁsargaṁ
bhaja sādhu-samāgamam
kuru puṇyam aho-rātraṁ
smara nityam anityatām
verses.synonyms: tyaja—renounce; durjana-saṁsargam—the association of demoniac persons; bhaja— partake of; sādhu-samāgamam—the association of devotees; kuru—perform; puṇyam—pious deeds; ahaḥ-rātram—both day and night; smara—remember; nityam—always; anityatām—the temporary nature of this world.
verses.translation: Renounce the company of evil-minded persons, associate with saintly persons, perform pious deeds both day and night, and remember always the temporary nature of this material world.

verses.title: Nīti Śāstra
verses.text:
varam eko guṇī putro
na ca mūrkha-śatair api
ekaś candras tamo hanti
na ca tārā-gaṇair api
verses.synonyms: varam—better; ekaḥ—one; guṇī—good qualities; putraḥ—a son; na—not; ca—and; mūrkha-śataiḥ—hundreds of fools; api—even; ekaḥ—one; candraḥ—moon; tamaḥ— darkness; hanti—destroys; na—not; ca—and; tārā-gaṇaiḥ—innumerable stars; api— even.
verses.translation: It is better to have one son with good qualities than to have one hundred foolish sons. Innumerable stars cannot dissipate the darkness, but one moon can illuminate the darkness of night.

verses.title: Nīti Śāstra
verses.text:
viśvāso naiva kartavyaḥ
strīṣu rāja-kuleṣu ca
verses.synonyms: viśvāsaḥ—trust; na—never; eva—certainly; kartavyaḥ—should be done; strīṣu— unto a woman; rāja-kuleṣu—a politician; ca—and.
verses.translation: On can never trust a politician or a woman.

verses.title: Nīti Śāstra
verses.text:
rṇa-kartā pita śatrur
mātā ca vyabhicāriṇī
bhāryā rūpavatī śatruḥ
putraḥ śatrur apaṇḍitaḥ
verses.synonyms: rṇa-kartā—a debtor; pita—father; śatruḥ—an enemy; mātā—mother; ca—also; vyabhicārinī—unfaithful; bhāryā—wife; rūpavatī—beautiful; śatruḥ—an enemy; putraḥ—a son; śatruḥ—enemy; apaṇḍitaḥ—ignorant.
verses.translation: There are four kinds of enemies in household life: a father who is a debtor, an unchaste wife, a wife who is beautiful, and a foolish, ignorant son.

verses.title: Nīti Śāstra
verses.text: śaṭhe śāṭhyamācareta
verses.synonyms: śaṭhe—in a cheating situation (i.e. when dealing with a cheat); śāṭhyama—like a cheat; ācareta—one should behave.
verses.translation: Śrīla Prabhupāda: This is politics, "Tit for tat." Śaṭhe śāṭhyamācareta. Cāṇakya Paṇḍita says. "If somebody is śaṭha"-śaṭha means very cunning-"so you should be also cunning."

verses.title: Carvaka Muni
verses.text:
ṛṇaṁ kṛtvā ghṛtaṁ pibet
yāvaj jīvet sukhaṁ jīvet
bhasmī-bhūtasya dehasya kutaḥ
punar āgamano bhavet
verses.synonyms: ṛṇam kṛtvā—going into debt; ghṛtam—ghee; pibet—one should eat; yāvaj—so long as; jīvet—one may live; sukham—happily; jīvet—he should live; bhasmī-bhūtasya—of that which becomes ashes; dehasya—of the body; kutaḥ—how; punaḥ—again; āgamanaḥ—coming; bhavet—will be.
verses.translation: Even if one has to go into debt, as long as one lives, he should live happily by eating as much ghee as possible. Since the material body simply becomes ashes at death, how will it ever come to life again?

verses.title: Ramakrishna
verses.text: yata mata, tata patha
verses.synonyms: yata—as many; mata—opinions; tata—that many; patha—ways.
verses.translation: There are as many paths as there are opinions.

verses.title: Unknown Source
verses.text:
bhajan kara sādhana kara
murte jānle hoy
verses.synonyms: bhajan—worship; kara—perform; sādhana—regulative devotional activities; kara— perform; murte—at the time of death; jānle—to know; hoy—is.
verses.translation: Whatever bhajana and sadhana one has performed throughout life will be tested at the time of death.

verses.title: Unknown Source
verses.text: bhāṣyaṁ brahma-sūtrānām
verses.synonyms: bhāṣyam—commentary; brahma-sūtrānām—on the Vedānta-sūtra.
verses.translation: The Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam is the (actual) commentary on the Vedānta-sūtra (Brahma-sūtra).

verses.title: Unknown Source
verses.text: punar mūṣiko bhava
verses.synonyms: punar—again; mūṣikaḥ—a mouse; bhava—become.
verses.translation: Again become a mouse.

verses.title: Unknown Source
verses.text: gavayā-dhanavān, dhānya-dhanavān
verses.synonyms: gavayā—cows; dhanavān—possessing wealth; dhānya—grains; dhanavān—possessing wealth.
verses.translation: One who has cows and grains possesses real wealth.

verses.title: Unknown Source
verses.text: hariṁ vinā mṛtiṁ na taranti
verses.synonyms: harim—Hari, the Supreme Personality of Godhead; vinā—without the grace of; mṛtim—death; na—not able; taranti—to cross over.
verses.translation: No one can overcome cruel death without the mercy of Hari, the Supreme Personality of Godhead.

verses.title: Unknown Source
verses.text:
janmanā jāyate śūdraḥ
saṁskarād bhaved dvijaḥ
veda-pāṭhād bhaved vipro
brahma jānātīti brāhmanaḥ
verses.synonyms: janmanā—by birth; jāyate—one is born; śūdraḥ—a śūdra; saṁskarāt—by the process of reformatory ceremonies such as initiation by a spiritual master; bhavet—one may become; dvijaḥ—twice-born brāhmaṇa; veda-pāṭhād—study of the Vedas; bhaved— one may become; vipro—a vipra (learned brāhmaṇa) brahma—the Supreme Spirit; jānātīti—knows; brāhmanaḥ—a brāhmaṇa.
verses.translation: By birth everyone is a śūdra, but by undergoing the purificatory ceremonies under the direction of a bona fide spiritual master, one may become a brāhmaṇa, and when one knows the Supreme Spirit, he actually becomes a truly learned brāhmaṇa.
verses.attribution: (Note: See Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam 1.12.29 for the difference between a brāhmaṇa and a

verses.title: Unknown Source
verses.text: vipra.)

verses.title: Unknown Source
verses.text: ghute pore gobar hase
verses.synonyms: ghute—dry cow dung paddy; pore—burns; gobar—wet cow dung paddy; hase—smiles.
verses.translation: When the dry cow dung is burning in the fire, the wet cow dung laughs.

verses.title: Unknown Source
verses.text:
janame janame sabe pitāmātā paya
kṛṣṇe guru nahi mile bhaja hari ei
verses.synonyms: janame janame—birth after birth; sabe—everybody; pitā—father; mātā—and mother; paya—gets; kṛṣṇe—Lord Kṛṣṇa; guru—spiritual master; nahi—do not; mile—come in contact with; bhaja—worship; hari—Lord Hari; ei—this.
verses.translation: Birth after birth one receives a mother and father, but if one gets the benediction of guru and Kṛṣṇa, he conquers the material energy and returns back to Godhead by worship of the Lord.

verses.title: Unknown Source
verses.text: pañcāś ordhvaṁ vanaṁ vrajet
verses.synonyms: pañcāś—fifty; ūrdhvam—above; vanam—forest; vrajet—one should go.
verses.translation: After the age of fifty years one should take vanaprastha and retire to the forest.

verses.title: Unknown Source
verses.text:
rākhe kṛṣṇa māre ke
māre kṛṣṇa rakhe ke
verses.synonyms: rākhe—protect; kṛṣṇa—Lord Kṛṣṇa; māre—kill; ke—who; māre—kill; kṛṣṇa— Kṛṣṇa; rakhe—protect; ke—who.
verses.translation: If Lord Kṛṣṇa protects a person, who can kill him? And if Kṛṣṇa desires to kill someone, who can protect him?

verses.title: Unknown Source
verses.text: yoga indriya saṁyama
verses.synonyms: yoga—the practice of yoga; indriya—the senses; saṁyama—to control.
verses.translation: Yoga practice means to control the senses.

verses.title: Unknown Source
verses.text:
rāja-putra cirañ jīva mā jīva muni putraka
jīva vā maro sādhur mā jīva marā iti
verses.synonyms: rāja-putra—O prince; cirat—a long time; jīva—live; mā jīva—do notlive; muni—a sage; putraka—O son; jīva—live; vā—or; maro—die; sādhur—O saintly person; mā jīva—do not live; marā—die; iti—thus.
verses.translation: O prince, may you live a long life; my dear brahmacārī, may you die now; O saintly person, you may live or die; but you, O butcher, don't live or die.

verses.title: Unknown Source
verses.text:
gṛhe śatrum api prāptaṁ
viśvastam akutobhayam
verses.synonyms: gṛhe—home; śatrum—enemy; api—if; prāptam—receive; viśvastam—trust; akutobhayam—without fear.
verses.translation: Even if your enemy comes to your home, you should receive him in such a way that he'll forget that you are his enemy.

verses.title: Unknown Source
verses.text: yasmin tuṣṭe jagat tuṣṭam
verses.synonyms: yasmin—to Him; tuṣṭe—satisfied; jagat—the whole world; tuṣṭam—satisfied.
verses.translation: If the Supreme Personality of Godhead is satisfied, everyone is satisfied.

verses.title: Unknown Source
verses.text: asaṅgo hy ayaṁ puruṣaḥ
verses.synonyms: asaṅgaḥ—not connected to the material world; hi—certainly; ayam—this; puruṣaḥ—the living entity.
verses.translation: The living entity is not really connected with this material world, but due to his tendency to enjoy the material senses he is put into a material condition.

verses.title: Unknown Source
verses.text: ātyantika-duḥkha-nivṛtti
verses.synonyms: ātyantika—ultimate; duḥkha—suffering; nivṛtti—finish.
verses.translation: One's aim in life should be to stop suffering.

verses.title: Unknown Source
verses.text: yāvad artha-prayojanam
verses.synonyms: yāvad—as much as; artha—economic conditions; prayojanam—necessities.
verses.translation: We accept only as much material necessities as needed for advancing in Kṛṣṇa consciousness.

verses.title: Unknown Source
verses.text: sarve sukhino bhavantu
verses.synonyms: sarve—everyone; sukhino—happy; bhavantu—become.
verses.translation: Let everyone be happy.ii*

verses.title: Unknown Source
verses.text: bhāva-grāhī janārdana
verses.synonyms: bhāva—spiritual intention; grāhī—who is influenced; janārdana—Lord Kṛṣṇa, the maintainer of all people.
verses.translation: The Lord accepts the essence of a devotee's attitude.

verses.title: Unknown Source
verses.text: ātmavan manyate jagat
verses.synonyms: ātmavan—just like himself; manyate—thinks; jagat—the whole world.
verses.translation: Everyone thinks of others according to his own position.

verses.title: Unknown Source
verses.text:
caṇḍālo 'pi dvija-śreṣṭho
hari-bhakti-parāyaṇaḥ
hari-bhakti-vihīnaś ca
dvijo 'pi śvapacādhamaḥ
verses.synonyms: caṇḍāla—an outcaste, and untouchable (a dog-eater); api—even; dvija-śreṣṭha—the best of the twice-born (brāhmaṇas); hari-bhakti-parāyaṇaḥ—a person who has concluded that devotional service for Kṛṣṇa is the supreme activity (and is therefore absorbed in serving the Lord); hari-bhakti-vihīnaḥ—one devoid of devotional service; ca—and; dvija—(even if he is) twice-born; śvapaca—a person who cooks (and therefore eats) dogs; adhamaḥ—the lowest.
verses.translation: "Even if one is born in the family of a caṇḍāla, if one engages in the devotional service of the Lord, he becomes the best of brāhmaṇas. But even a brāhmaṇa who is devoid of devotional service is on the level of the lowest dog-eater."

verses.title: Sanskrit Proverb
verses.text:
satyaṁ brūyāt priyaṁ brūyāt
mā brūyāt satyam apriyam
verses.synonyms: satyam—truth; brūyāt—speak; priyam—pleasing; brūyāt—speak; mā—do not; brūyāt—speak; satyam—truth; apriyam—not pleasing.
verses.translation: If one speaks the truth, he should speak it palatably. One should not speak unpalatable truth.iii*

verses.title: Bengali Proverb
verses.text: andha-paṅgu-nyāya
verses.synonyms: andha—blind man; paṅgu—lame man; nyāya—logic.
verses.translation: The logic of the blind man and the lame man.

verses.title: Bengali Proverb
verses.text: tandula vṛścika nyāya
verses.synonyms: tandula—rice; vṛścika—scorpion; nyāya—logic.
verses.translation: The logic of the rice and the scorpion.

verses.title: Bengali Proverb
verses.text: kūpa-maṇḍūka-nyāya
verses.synonyms: kūpa—well; maṇḍūka—frog; nyāya—logic.
verses.translation: The logic of the frog in the well. principles, speaking truthfully, controlling the senses by undergoing austerities and penances, being free from jealousy, being intelligent, being tolerant, creating no enemies, performing yajña, giving charity, being steady, being well versed in Vedic study, and observing vows.
verses.attribution: iiiŚrīla Prabhupāda explains that this is only in relation to material truths.
